record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: For the disturbance-to-state stabilization of the considered linear hyperbolic PDE with dynamic boundary feedback, can the matrix inequality condition (5.52b) be relaxed or replaced by alternative criteria that still guarantee robustness? The broader goal is to enlarge the class of hyperbolic systems treatable by this controller-design approach.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.22. In the statement of Theorem 5.18, condition (5.52a) requires infD∈Dn+ kD(H +BK)D−1k < 1 which also appears in the more general context of nonlinear systems [43] when analyzing stability with respect to H2-norm. However, the condition (5.52b) is introduced in [215] to compensate for the lack of proportional gain in the feedback law. It definitely restricts the class of systems that can be treated with this approach and relaxing this condition or obtaining different criteria is a topic of further investigation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional linear hyperbolic system on the spatial domain $x\in[0,1]$,
$$\partial_t y(t,x) + \Lambda\, \partial_x y(t,x) = 0,\qquad t\ge 0,$$
where $y(t,\cdot)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ with $\lambda_i>0$. Assume a (dynamic) boundary feedback of the form
$$y(t,0)=H\,y(t,1)+B\,u(t)+d(t),\qquad \dot u(t)=K\,y(t,1),$$
where $H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, $B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, $K\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $u(t)\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is an internal controller state (so the feedback contains no direct proportional term on $y(t,1)$), and $d\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+;\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a disturbance. Let $\mathcal{D}_n^+$ denote the set of diagonal positive-definite $n\times n$ matrices, and for $D\in\mathcal{D}_n^+$ let $\|D(H+BK)D^{-1}\|$ denote the induced spectral norm.

A known sufficient condition for input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to $d$ in the $H^2$-norm consists of two matrix inequalities:
\begin{align}
\text{(C1)}\quad &\inf_{D\in\mathcal{D}_n^+}\|D(H+BK)D^{-1}\|<1,\\
\text{(C2)}\quad &\text{an additional matrix inequality on }(\Lambda,H,B,K)\text{ that compensates for the absence of a proportional term in the feedback.}
\end{align}

Problem: Determine whether condition (C2) can be relaxed or replaced by alternative verifiable criteria, jointly with (C1), that still guarantee input-to-state stability (with respect to $d$, in the $H^2$-norm) of the closed-loop system, so as to enlarge the class of triples $(\Lambda,H,B)$ (equivalently, the class of linear hyperbolic systems with dynamic boundary feedback of the above form) for which a stabilizing gain $K$ can be designed.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface any paper explicitly relaxing the auxiliary matrix inequality compensating for the missing proportional gain in the dynamic boundary feedback design for linear hyperbolic systems. The topic remains an active research area with related but distinct ISS results for hyperbolic PDE/PDE-ODE systems, and no resolution of the specific question was identified.

status_evidence.title: Boundary stabilization of 1D hyperbolic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of stabilization criteria for 1D hyperbolic systems using matrix inequality conditions and Lyapunov methods.
status_evidence.claim: Matrix-inequality criteria of the form inf_D ||D(H+BK)D^{-1}||<1 are standard sufficient conditions, but auxiliary conditions for dynamic (integral) feedback restrict the treatable class.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Boundary Stabilization of First Order Hyperbolic Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces dynamic boundary controllers for first-order hyperbolic systems and the additional matrix conditions required.
status_evidence.claim: The supplementary matrix inequality used to compensate for the lack of proportional gain in dynamic boundary feedback restricts the applicable class of systems.
